content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: shift breaks, add callback and keep the outage message running. Predicted 86.7% service level for 13:00–15:00 at no extra cost.","why":"The extra payments calls are most likely caused by the card authorisation gateway outage (P1 incident INC-20261016-7996, opened 11:45). Card_declined calls ran at 4.95x normal and account for about 228 of the roughly 287 excess calls. Service level fell as low as 10.1% at 12:15. P1 is predicted to reach 86.7% over 13:00–15:00, against the 80% target, with payments at 88.1% and general at 84.3%. Abandons are predicted at 3.2%. It costs nothing extra and breaks no policy rules. Rest-of-day service level is predicted at 91.8%.","trade_offs":["Doing nothing (P0) is also predicted to meet target, at 84.0% with 3.8% abandons. That leaves less margin, with general at 81.7%. P1 adds headroom at the same zero cost.","P2 gives a higher 91.7% (2.6% abandons, rest of day 95.0%) for ₹552, using chat deflection. It is worth considering if you want a bigger buffer.","P3 is strongest at 95.5% with 1.3% abandons, but costs ₹3,672 in overtime for 30 agents. P4 reaches 89.4% for ₹1,440.","P1's rest-of-day figure (91.8%) is slightly below P0's (92.3%), likely because breaks move later and callbacks are handled afterwards.","Under P1, general is the weaker queue at 84.3%, because general breaks are also delayed. It stays above target."],"watch":"Track the incident status and card_declined volume. If the outage runs beyond 15:00 or general service level drops toward 80%, step up to P2 (₹552). Also confirm the delayed breaks and the callback backlog are cleared after 15:00."}
